question: Public health services remained largely inaccessible to the masses during the colonial rule. What was India's approximate life expectancy at the time of independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**30-32 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India’s life expectancy at the time of independence in 1947 was approximately **30-32 years**.
 
• The low life expectancy was attributed to widespread poverty, lack of healthcare facilities, and high prevalence of infectious diseases like malaria, cholera, and tuberculosis.
 
• During the colonial era, public health services were **highly inadequate**, especially in rural areas, leading to high mortality rates.
 
• Infant mortality and maternal mortality rates were also alarmingly high due to poor medical infrastructure and lack of proper nutrition.
 
• Post-independence, significant improvements in healthcare and living standards contributed to a gradual increase in life expectancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Life Expectancy:** It refers to the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on demographic factors like healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition.
 
• **Colonial Healthcare System:** During British rule, healthcare was largely focused on protecting the colonial administration and urban elites, leaving the rural population underserved.
 
• **Post-Independence Initiatives:** India introduced major public health programs such as the National Malaria Eradication Program (1953) and family planning initiatives to improve public health metrics.
 
• **Current Trends:** As of 2023, India’s life expectancy has increased to approximately **69-70 years**, reflecting advancements in healthcare and living conditions.
 
• **Global Comparison:** In 1947, India’s life expectancy was among the lowest globally, but consistent efforts in healthcare have significantly improved its ranking over the decades.
